statement.excerpt: This is one of the core issues with measuring AI demand — that the vast majority of it comes from selling services that do not make any economic sense.

from_speaker: selling services that do not make any economic sense
our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion gives this otherwise evaluative phrase a testable reading: commercial AI spending predominantly supports services whose delivery costs exceed customer payments.
Measure demand by spending, because the argument concerns revenue and compute purchases. Do not substitute user counts or token volumes.
Use Q3 2026, the latest completed quarter before the post, for this ongoing observation.
Vast majority means a clear, large majority; the speaker supplies no defensible exact cutoff.
Company-wide losses, introductory subsidies, and losses on unusually heavy users do not by themselves establish negative economics across a service's customer base.
Avoid counting the same customer payment repeatedly as it passes through application providers, model labs, and infrastructure suppliers.
criteria.support_condition: Representative, spending-weighted evidence shows that a clear, large majority of commercial AI demand is generated by services whose aggregate delivery costs exceed their customer payments.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence shows that most commercial AI spending is associated with services covering their delivery costs, leaving the asserted large majority untenable.
